sections.title: Studies in Digital Media: The Cabinet of Vanishing Landscapes
sections.description: his course introduces students to historical and contemporary techniques of environmental rendering that merge art, science, and speculation. Students will extrapolate on the 20th-century technique of habitat dioramas, using the Academy of Natural Sciences as a primary reference. They will explore how dioramas offer ghostly historical snapshots of otherwise dynamic ecosystems, while proposing how this format can be updated to imagine future climate scenarios. With digital modeling and game engines as their main tools, students will reconstruct the unique combination of geology, soil, vegetation, and megafauna represented in habitat dioramas. They will conduct detailed research on how climate forecasts might affect these habitats, and ultimately project their dioramas into an unknown and unknowable future. No prior experience with these tools is required, only a willingness to learn by testing, making, and iterating. The anticipated material budget is roughly $80 per student.
